newsitem.title: FINLAND: STOCKMANN PLANS NEW MOSCOW DEPT STORE.
newsitem.headline: STOCKMANN PLANS NEW MOSCOW DEPT STORE.

text.p: Finnish retail and department store group Stockmann said in a statement on Tuesday it had signed a letter of intent to open a new 6,700 square metre department store in central Moscow next spring.
"The sales target for the first year is a good 300 million markka, which means doubling Stockmann's current sales in Russia," Stockmann said.
The investment in refurbishing the rented property would be about 50 million markka, it said.
Stockmann said the project was pending fulfilment of some conditions by end-September.
Stockmann's department store would be part the Smolenski Passage business centre, less than two kilometres from the Kremlin, and it was planned to be "an anchor" for the whole shopping site, it said.
Some 5,000 square metres of Stockmann's premises would be shopping area, it said.
Stockmann said it was the first western retailer to have established itself in Moscow by opening a store in 1989, and that it now had four shops there.
"The small sizes and partly difficult locations have impeded developing the trade to become more department-store-like," it said.
Stockmann's Moscow operations are part of its foreign business which include a food outlet in St Petersburg and a department store and a clothing retail outlet in Estonia.
The foreign business' 1996 net sales totalled 412 million markka, it said. Total group net sales were 6.16 billion markka.
